newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down at intra-day low vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down at intra-day low vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan moved up early on Monday due to the growth of China's trade surplus and a lower interest rate subsidy, but finally ended the session down on profit-taking, traders said.
The yuan closed at an intra-day low of 8.3001 on Monday against the U.S. dollar from last Friday's 8.2990 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
The official media reported that China had a trade surplus of about $2 billion for November and $14 billion for the first 11 months of 1996.
The People's Bank of China also announced the January interest rate subsidy on bank deposits of three years or more at 2.87 percent, down from 3.72 percent for December.
Dealers said both items of news were positive factors for the yuan's uptrend and pushed the yuan up in today's early trading.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2990 and consolidated up to hit an intra-day high of 8.2981 before falling slightly late in the session to close at a low.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.2995, traders said.

"Increases in China's trade surplus implied more dollar selling in the market, which supported the yuan," one dealer said. "The lower interest rate subsidy also reflected better controls over inflation which pushed the yuan up early in the session."
"The rise in the yuan was halted by profit-taking on expectation that it would not rise further," said a second dealer.
"Most people do not think the yuan will move far away from the key 8.3000 level before the end of this year," he added.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.3000 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at 7.2600 from 7.3350 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intra-day high of 1.0720 from 1.0730 against the Hong Kong dollar.
